project_comments.note: Architectural observation (src/plugins/runner.ts): runPartials() and runPersonaPartials() assign each plugin's hook return value directly to `accumulated` with no nullish guard. A JavaScript plugin (or a typed plugin using a type-cast workaround) that inadvertently returns undefined would corrupt `accumulated`, causing all subsequent plugins and the partial resolution step to crash. The TypeScript type signatures (`onPartials?(...): Record<string,string>`) prevent this at compile time for well-typed consumers, but the runtime path is unprotected. Recommended fix: `accumulated = plugin.onPartials(accumulated, suiteName, suite) ?? accumulated` (same pattern for onPersonaPartials). This is pre-existing behavior not introduced by any WP in this project — surfaced during WP-008 code review.

project_comments.note: Cross-cutting synthesis observation: The null-guard gap in all accumulating runners (runPartials, runPersonaPartials, runBuildContext, runPostRender in src/plugins/runner.ts) is the single highest-priority follow-up from this project. Each runner assigns the plugin hook return value directly to `accumulated` with no nullish fallback. A plugin returning undefined would corrupt the accumulated map for all subsequent plugins and crash the build at resolvePartials/resolveVariables. Recommended fix for all four functions: `accumulated = plugin.onHook(...) ?? accumulated`. This pattern was surfaced four separate times across WP-004, WP-005, WP-008, and the WP-008 code review, and was elevated to a project-level architectural comment by the Reviewer. The fix is < 4 lines of code and eliminates a class of hard-to-diagnose runtime failures. Should be the first item in the next implementation sprint.
